critique.reason: The proposal's $3,000 is wrong. Under MSA-NW-2025 §4.2, the credit is 0.5% of the monthly fee ($500) per full hour of unavailability beyond the §4.1 commitment, and the total for any calendar month may not exceed $1,000. The cap controls the result. Even on the most generous reading, six full hours at $500 is $3,000, which the cap reduces to $1,000. The proposal also ignores the 99.9% monthly availability allowance: September 2026 has 720 hours, so about 43 minutes of downtime is permitted. TCK-881 records 6h15m of unavailability, which leaves roughly 5.5 hours beyond the commitment (five full hours, or $2,500 before the cap). Either way the supported credit is $1,000. The request was made in writing on 2026-09-26, within 30 days of the 2026-09-14 incident, so the credit is valid. The customer's $3,000 deduction is a set-off, which §7.4 prohibits except for a §4.2 credit. Only the $1,000 credit may be applied. The remaining $2,000 of INV-1001 is still owed. The invoice was due 2026-10-01 under Net 30, so it is now past due, and §3.2 late-payment accrual of 1% per month may apply. The credit memo should be issued for $1,000 and the $2,000 shortfall pursued as an unpaid balance. CRM-2210 was reviewed and does not change the contractual amount.
